section_1.title: The Hook: The Musical Analogy
section_1.content: Introduce the concept that any complex periodic signal is just a chord made of pure notes. Prerequisites: Familiarity with basic trigonometry (sine and cosine waves). Visual: A chaotic wave flattening into a layered stack of simple, smooth sine waves.
section_1.example: A smart cat's purr: Analyzing how the complex rumble is actually a combination of a fundamental 'base' frequency and higher-pitched harmonics.

section_2.title: The Core Concept: Defining Fourier Series
section_2.content: Define the Fourier Series as a decomposition of a periodic function f(x) into an infinite sum of sines and cosines. Emphasize that the coefficients (a_n, b_n) represent the 'weight' or intensity of each frequency component.
section_2.example: A light-mixing console where each slider (harmonic) changes the shape of the output wave.

section_3.title: Visualizing Coefficients: The Integration Trick
section_3.content: Explain the orthogonality of sines and cosines. Use the 'Inner Product' concept to show how we 'sift' out specific frequencies. Visual: An animation of a filter sliding over a wave, isolating one specific sine component.
section_3.example: A radio tuner: Turning the knob (calculating the coefficient) to isolate a specific signal from the static of the airwaves.

section_4.title: Step-by-Step Construction: Synthesis
section_4.content: Show the additive process. Starting with the fundamental frequency (n=1), add n=2, n=3... up to n=infinity. Visual: A square wave emerging as we sum more sine terms, showing the 'Gibbs phenomenon' at sharp edges.
section_4.example: A 3D printer nozzle tracing a square path; the motors combine simple back-and-forth movements to create a rigid, sharp-cornered shape.

section_5.title: Conclusion & Application
section_5.content: Summarize the transformation from Time Domain to Frequency Domain. Connect this to modern technology. Visual: A split screen showing a heartbeat signal (time) vs. its clean pulse spectrum (frequency).
section_5.example: Noise-canceling headphones: A device that uses Fourier analysis to detect background drone frequencies and injects the 'negative' phase to neutralize them instantly.
